Revised assessment incorporating the literature: The FOMC’s “hold” at 4.25–4.50% with continued balance‑sheet runoff and IORB at 4.4% signals a risk‑management stance that is broadly consistent with Taylor‑rule guidance when inflation is above target and slack is limited (Federal Reserve follows/implements Taylor rule; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). The cautious tone (“uncertainty… remains elevated”) is balanced by credible commitment to the 2% objective and attention to expectations—core elements of inflation‑forecast targeting and optimal policy under commitment (Svensson and Woodford, 2003/2004; FOMC targets PCE inflation). Ongoing QT and reliance on administered rates (interest on reserves, ON RRP) keep financial conditions relatively tight and can affect term premia via the yield curve (Cochrane and Piazzesi; FRBNY operations), which is mildly hawkish. However, two dovish dissents (preferring a 25 bp cut) and acknowledgement of moderated growth soften the overall tone. Netting these, the statement reads slightly negative but closer to neutral than the prior −0.15.
